items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...they had the Avery Tillman orchestra, they were Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman and Dude... [INTERVIEWEE] take the trumpet down. And Tillman would play the lead.

ctx.x: Tyler's Beer Garden, when I first came to town, they had the Avery Tillman orchestra, they were Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman and Dude. Joe Avery, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. And all that time that I'd hear them, the trumpet would play that lead and Avery would be popping away there, you know. Oh, yeah, he was strong for Tillman. Yeah, and then Dude would take down, you know,
take the trumpet down. And Tillman would play the lead. He'd play a lead all the way,

most of the time. Yeah. Right with the trumpet. Well, Tillman would take the lead part of the time. Part of the time, man. And then Joe would accompany him, but there would never be a real solo, there was just a trumpet would take down would be all. No, no, and he'd play right on through. Were there many bands like that in the old days? No, they worked that way too. They worked that way too, in addition to having the solos. Played right on through. And you say there are less solos then and now.
